svg.text: times in hours and minutes · heights in metres · the Admiralty method
TIME DIFFERENCES, at the standard port times in its row
14 ports: no differences here. Use the SOLENT SPECIAL CURVES, referred to LW Portsmouth.
no tidal data: the RAM gives no low waters here and FES does not fit — see note *
TIMES: over the HW and LW columns, each STANDARD PORT row gives the times its high and low water fall at springs and at neaps (0000 and 1200 are one column).
Interpolate a time difference by the time of that day's HW or LW at the standard port, between those columns. HEIGHTS: by that day's HW or LW height, between the levels in its row.

Beyond the levels, carry the height difference on in the same proportion: extrapolate it. The time difference stays between its columns. Round each to the minute and the tenth, add them, and between HW and LW use the standard port's curve.
SOURCE, the small letter on the right. M measured: analysed from a tide gauge at the port or within 3 M; checked against the water: Brighton 16 cm and 5 min, Honfleur 27 cm and 20 min.

R RAM: from the levels and establishment published by the Shom (RAM, Licence Ouverte 2.0); expected error 0.536 per mile to the standard port + 5.9 cm and 0.190 per mile + 10.9 min, more in estuaries.
F FES: from the FES2022 tide model (CNES/LEGOS/NOVELTIS/CLS, AVISO), modified: model differences, not measured; expected error 42 cm and 21 min against the ports that have a tide gauge.
* Saint-Valery-sur-Somme: this training almanac has no tidal data for it. Heights above chart datum. Not for navigation.
